units.text: INT. STARLIGHT ROLLER RINK - NIGHT
A mirror ball turns slowly over a dead floor.
Dust lies on the skate rental counter.
Somewhere an old organ wheezes a note and stops.
CORNELIUS "NEIL" PRATT, fifties, in a rumpled suit, carries a lantern and a ledger.
MILDRED ASHCROFT, sixties, his realtor, follows in a tweed coat with her keys held like a weapon.
FITZ, a lean teenager with a flashlight and a tool bag, brings up the rear.
Mildred, you said the power was off.
units.name: NEIL

units.text: It is, Neil.
units.name: MILDRED

units.text: Then who is playing the organ?
units.name: NEIL

units.text: The building settles. It makes noises.
units.name: MILDRED

units.text: Fitz crouches by the wall and pokes at a fuse box.
He whistles through his teeth, a tuneless little line.
Mr. Pratt, the box is cold. Dead for years.
units.name: FITZ

units.text: All three turn.
At the far end of the rink, a pair of skates, white leather, laces tied, sits at the edge of the floor, as if someone has just stepped out of them.
Mildred takes a step back.
Neil steps forward and lifts his lantern.
Fitz swings his flashlight at the skates and holds it there, the beam very steady.
Those weren't there when we came in.
units.name: NEIL

units.text: Nonsense. They were.
units.name: MILDRED

units.text: Mildred, they weren't.
units.name: FITZ

units.text: Nobody moves.
The mirror ball turns.
Spots of light cross their faces, one after another.
The skates slide a few inches toward them across the floor, wheels humming.
Neil, Mildred, and Fitz stop breathing together.
The wheels go quiet.
Well. We'll note it in the listing.
units.name: MILDRED

units.text: She writes in her notebook, her pen perfectly smooth.
Neil sets down the lantern.
Fitz, go and check the doors.
units.name: NEIL

units.text: They're locked, sir. From outside.
units.name: FITZ

units.text: The organ plays one low chord.
The three of them stay where they are, watching the skates, which do not move again.
